newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Murdoch clears last Super League legal hurdle.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Murdoch clears last Super League legal hurdle.

text.p: The Australian Rugby League (ARL) were refused special leave on Friday to appeal against media baron Rupert Murdoch's recent Federal Court victory, enabling his breakaway Super League to kick off next year.

The decision closes the avenues of appeal and means it is virtually certain there will be two rival leagues next season, with the ARL premiership in direct competition with Super League, backed by Murdoch's News Ltd, the Australian arm of News Corp Ltd.
ARL lawyer Bob Ellicott submitted that the High Court should intervene as a matter of public interest because the earlier Full Bench of the Federal Court ruling was wrong.
After a hearing lasting one hour, the three High Court judges adjourned for 15 minutes before rejecting the ARL's appeal, saying there were no new grounds to warrant it.
The application was opposed by News Ltd, Brisbane Broncos and a group of more than 300 players.

The Federal Court last month ruled that the five-year loyalty agreements between the ARL and 20 clubs, including the Broncos, breached trade practices legislation. The ruling freed rebel clubs to play under the Super League banner next year.
